name: NC-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+24 partisan baseline)
Incumbent Alma Adams running for reelection with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger is minimally funded with almost no cash on hand
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%
model.rationale: This Charlotte-area seat leans heavily Democratic, Adams is an entrenched incumbent with a dominant fundraising position, and her opponent has raised under $30,000 with essentially no cash on hand. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic win.
model.watch: Only an unexpected late outside-spending surge for the Republican challenger or a major scandal involving Adams would put the margin in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 12th District is a heavily Democratic, majority-Black Charlotte-area seat, and Alma Adams has held it comfortably since 2014. She is running for reelection with about $457,000 on hand, while Republican Jack Codiga has raised under $30,000 and reports almost no cash remaining, leaving him little capacity to compete.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong partisan lean, the incumbency advantage, and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets price Adams near 97%, consistent with a safe Democratic seat. A Republican upset would require a dramatic shift well beyond anything visible in the current evidence.
